subject: Optimize toolkit packaging & quant/batching guidance — LedgerAI procurement
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@ledgerai.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@ledgerai.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Initial inquiry — Optimize toolkit packaging + quant recommendations

Hi Chloe,

Hope you’re well. I’m Sanjay, leading procurement at LedgerAI. We’ve been evaluating Redwood’s Optimize toolkit for inference cost reductions — specifically batching/caching guidance and recommended quantization profiles for customer-facing latency under 150ms. Our usage profile (rough numbers):
- Avg tokens/day: ~350M tokens (peak 1.1B on heavy days)
- Mix: 60% short-chat (<=64 tokens), 40% long-form generation (avg 512 tokens)
- Current latency targets: p95 <= 150ms for short-chat, p95 <= 400ms for long-form acceptable

Before we schedule an SRE/SE deep-dive, can you:
1) Share recommended quantization options that balance latency vs. hallucination risk for these mixes
2) Outline packaging/discount flexibility (pilot vs committed) — we may be open to a 12-month commit if economics justify it
3) Call out any caveats around caching (privacy, warm-up misses) and how that affects billing/credits

Looking to get a ballpark commercial range and technical guardrails so we can scope an internal approval.

Thanks — Sanjay
Procurement
LedgerAI

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@ledgerai.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, procurement@ledgerai.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial inquiry — Optimize toolkit packaging + quant recommendations

Hi Sanjay — great to meet you over email. Thanks for the clear usage snapshot.

Short answers up front:
- Quantization: for a mixed workload like yours we usually recommend an int8 (GPT-style aware) profile for short-chat and a mixed int8/int4 strategy for long-form where we can tolerate slightly more variance but gain cost.
- Batching/Caching: Enable prefix KV caching for short-chat conversational flows (can reduce repeated prefix compute by ~25-55% depending on heat). Adaptive batching with a 12-25ms micro-batching window typically preserves p95 for short responses.
- Packaging: we can offer a 12-month committed tier with tiered discounts (higher commit -> deeper discount). We also provide limited pilot credits to validate the topology and a technical appendix that explains tradeoffs.

I’ve attached a one-page commercial sketch and a short technical appendix (attached). If it’s helpful I can loop in Connor for a concise technical run-through and Kimberly for commercial terms.

As a couple of clarifying Qs before Connor dives deeper:
- How many distinct models/prompt templates will you serve? (KV cache effectiveness depends on template reuse)
- What % of requests include large tool calls or external blocking steps? (affects batching windows)

Proposed next step: 30-min SE call this week to validate caching/quant gains; then we’ll send a scoped proposal. Would Thu 5/13 10am PT work?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: optimize_pricing_v1.pdf (PDF), quant-batching-tech-appendix.md (MD)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Initial inquiry — Optimize toolkit packaging + quant recommendations

Hi Sanjay / Chloe — Connor from SE. Quick technical notes from what you shared:

1) Quantization approach (risk / reward):
- Short-chat: int8 (dynamic range-aware) is our pragmatic default. Minimal deltas in output quality for most assistant tasks; gives ~2.3x throughput improvement on A100-like hardware versus fp16.
- Long-form: evaluate int8 with per-layer calibration; for particularly brittle prompts we recommend a fallback path that serves a small fraction (1-3%) on fp16 to detect regressions for critical UX flows.

2) Caching & cache effectiveness:
- If you have high template reuse (>40%) KV cache can cut token cost by 20-50% (we see variance by session stickiness).
- Privacy: KV cache respects TTL/eviction and can be disabled per-route. For regulated content we recommend caching only on Dedicated/Private with customer-managed KMS.

3) Batching strategy to meet latency SLOs:
- Micro-batching window: 12-20ms for p95 <=150ms on short-chat when combined with async prefix caching.
- For long-form, batch sizes up to 8-12 tokens per request help throughput without blowing p95 if you allow 200-400ms windows.

4) Operational counterpoints:
- Warm-up misses: first N requests post-deploy will not hit cache; factor into pilot credit planning.
- Autoscale burst: ensure dedicated pool headroom or we’ll route to compatible lower-cost variants with clear FIFO fallback.

I’ll share a small simulation sheet if you can confirm: avg short-chat tokens per request, avg long-form tokens per request (you gave 512), and sample concurrency. That will let us produce a modeled cost delta for int8+cache vs fp16 baseline.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Sanjay — Kimberly here, pricing lead. Following Chloe and Connor’s notes, here’s a commercial path that balances downside protection for LedgerAI and runway for Redwood to invest in the integration:

Proposal (starter economics):
- 12-month committed agreement: $180k/month committed consumption (billed monthly). Commitment equates to a blended discount of ~22% vs hosted list when using recommended int8 + KV cache profile.
- Ramp & pilot credits: 6 weeks of pilot credits (~$25k value) applied during onboarding to compensate warm-up/cache tuning.
- Upside sharing: If LedgerAI exceeds 1.5x committed consumption, overage is billed at list-minus-10% for the next band.
- Technical credits: include two SE onsite/remote workshops (up to 8 hours) and assistance with quant calibration.

A few contract notes:
- Price protection for 12 months; we can include a 60-day exit for material SLA failure.
- For data residency/privacy constraints we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments — those can be added as a SKUs and priced separately.

Next steps:
1) If the numbers look directionally OK, Chloe will set a short contract call to agree terms and finalize SOW scope.
